chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid and Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr; and Faḍālah, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Ibn Muskān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān, all together from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a man who was in...

a cold land, and he fears that if he performs ghusl, some hardship from the ghusl will afflict him—what should he do? He عليه السلام said: He should perform ghusl, even if what may afflict him does afflict him. He said: And he mentioned that he had been suffering severe pain, then janabah befell him while he was in a cold place, and it was a very windy, cold night. So I called the servants and said to them: Carry me and wash me. They said: We fear for you. So I said: There is no alternative. Thus they carried me, placed me upon planks, then poured water over me and washed me.

key_terms.أَرْضٍ بَارِدَةٍ: a cold land or environment causing physical hardship
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.لَيْلَةٌ شَدِيدَةُ الرِّيحِ بَارِدَةٌ: an intensely windy and cold night

ai.seo_question: What should a junub person do if he fears hardship from performing ghusl in extreme cold?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a person in janabah who is in intense cold and fears harm from ghusl. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that ghusl is to be performed, and supports this by recounting his own experience of enduring severe pain and cold conditions in order to undergo ritual washing.
